verdict.line: You lose if Fiora lands Q (Lunge) onto your Vitals and chains the refresh dash before you can hop away; you win if you poke her down with ranged Q (Boomerang Throw) before she's in melee range.

brief.thesis: This is an even matchup on paper (46% Gnar win rate over 1539 games) but it plays out as a range-vs-melee duel: Mini Gnar wants to throw Boomerang Throw and kite with Hyper's move speed, while Fiora wants to close the gap with Q (Lunge) and parry your engage with W (Riposte). The fight only gets scary for you once she's already on top of you, so your entire job is denying that first dash.

theirWindow.when: she has both Q (Lunge) charges up
theirWindow.what: She can dash twice within a couple seconds at no mana cost, closing nearly 1200 range instantly. Do not stand still in minion-clear range or walk a straight line toward her — she'll land both hits and start stacking her passive (Duelist) healing off you.

yourWindow.when: her Q (Lunge) is on cooldown (8-16s depending on rank)
yourWindow.what: Walk up and land ranged Boulder Toss/Boomerang Throw pokes — she has no way to close the distance or escape your Q's slow. This is your only real damage window before level 6, so use it every time her dash is down.

powerCurve.note: Neither side all-ins; trade pokes if Q is up
Boomerang slow kites her Lunge engages
Blade Waltz threatens burst if you're mega and stuck
Trinity Force spike lets you match her duels
Black Cleaver + Sterak's outscale her single-target kit

start.why: Picked 58.2% of the time and posts a 46.3% win rate over 1083 games — the lifesteal and AD help you win the poke trades that define this lane before her Q is online every fight.

boots.why: Run in 90.4% of games (46.9% win rate) — the reduced auto-attack damage specifically blunts her Burst of Speed (E) attack-speed windows and her auto-reliant Blade Waltz (R) hits.

core.why: The core first item in 22.5-10.4% of builds depending on third slot — the move speed and burst proc let Mini Gnar poke-and-reposition before she can close with Q (Lunge).
Second item in every major build path — the armor shred compounds her Duelist sustain problem and helps your autos and Boulder Toss hit harder through her stacking Overgrowth health.
Most popular third item (59.8% win rate over 204 games) — the shield absorbs exactly the kind of burst her Blade Waltz (R) delivers if she ever does land it.

situational.when: she's snowballing and landing Blade Waltz (R) for free
she's building full lifesteal/Duelist stacking and you need the sustain cut
you need an early answer to her passive healing before Black Cleaver is done

runes.keystoneWhy: Run in 34.6% of games at a 47.5% win rate — the sustain and move speed on poke trades directly counter her all-in plan, since you're never meant to let her get the first hit.

summoners.why: The most-run combo at 64.5% pick and 45.4% win rate — Teleport lets you reset after poke trades and keep pressure on the wave without worrying about her punishing a recall, since this is a long, patient lane rather than a kill lane.

playing.title: Poke only when her Q is down
playing.detail: Track her Q (Lunge) cooldown (8-16s by rank) on screen. If it's up, back off — she can double-dash onto you for free. If it's down, step up and land Boomerang Throw or an auto before retreating.

playing.title: Never auto into her raised W
playing.detail: Riposte (W) parries your next basic attack and reflects magic damage, and increases her AD on activation. If you see her trigger it, hold your autos and your empowered Hyper attack for 1-2 seconds until it expires.

playing.title: Save your E for her Q, not for poke
playing.detail: Hop (E, 12-22s cooldown by rank) is your only way to escape a double Lunge. Don't burn it to extend a trade unless you're certain you can kill her — if she still has Q up, you need the bounce to disengage.

playing.title: Respect Blade Waltz once she's 6
playing.detail: From level 6 on, don't get caught alone at low HP even outside her Lunge range — Blade Waltz (R) has 400 range and dashes to you regardless of minions. Ward your flanks and don't overextend past her Q threat range when her ultimate is up (90-130s cooldown).

playing.title: Transform away from her dash, not into it
playing.detail: When you hit max Rage and are about to transform, try to do it after dodging a Lunge, not while standing still — Mega Gnar loses Hyper's kite speed and instead gets Wallop's stun, which only works if she's already committed into melee range.

playing.title: Use mega form's E to punish her E window
playing.detail: If she pops Burst of Speed (E) to stick to you, your Mega Gnar Crunch (E) deals area damage around you on landing — time your transform so the knockdown lands while she's still in attack range, since she can't escape it the way she dodges Mini Gnar's bounce.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner picks are pulled directly from measured OP.GG data on patch 16.19.1 across 1500+ games; the trade-pattern and ability-timing reasoning above is my own analysis layered on top of those numbers.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of having your Vitals hit with (Q). Avoid being hit with (W) when you use [R]. Purchase Executioner’s Calling.
